title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck's notes on the motivic Galois group (cote 15). The page sits among unrelated Bourbaki drafts on point distributions and was apparently written on their versos. It sketches how the motivic Galois group G (or its identity component G°), attached to motives over a number field K, carries the Hodge realization at each place of K, plus the extra structure at real places.

Modern reading of the first block. V is a G°-module, i.e. a motive seen through a Betti-type Q-fibre functor, and V_C = V ⊗_Q C. An archimedean place ξ of K (a complex embedding) provides three things.
(i) A K-subspace H_ξ(V) ⊂ V_C. This is the de Rham realization, which is a K-form, embedded in V_C by the comparison isomorphism.
(ii) A decreasing filtration H_ξ(V)^{(p)} (the Hodge filtration), defined over K.
(iii) After extending scalars, H_ξ(V)^{(p)}_C makes V a Hodge structure, possibly in families ('variation de structures de Hodge' / 'faisceau de Hodge'). The group of this Hodge structure, its Mumford–Tate group, is G°. More precisely, the image of G° in GL(V).

Second block, restated for a general place ξ of K. The completions K_{ξ1}, K_{ξ2}, … over K over Q are drawn as a tree. One has V̄_ξ = V ⊗_Q K̄_ξ ⊃ H_ξ(V)^{(p)}. The H_ξ(V)^p ⊗_K K_ξ define a Hodge structure on the pair (V, V_K), with Galois group Im G°. This is essentially the Deligne-style system of realizations (Betti, de Rham over K, comparison, Hodge filtration), with Mumford–Tate group equal to the image of the motivic Galois group.

Real places. If ξ is real, there is an involution of V coming from an element Frob_ξ ∈ G(Q), the 'Frobenius at infinity' F_∞. He asks that it be compatible with a hermitian form on V̄_ξ (polarization) and that 'Frob_ξ' be the identity on H_ξ(V), hence compatible with the Hodge structure. In modern terms these are the real Hodge structures with F_∞ used by Deligne in 'Valeurs de fonctions L et périodes d'intégrales' (1979).

The marginal remark 'notion de Deligne' (reading uncertain) suggests the page dates from after Deligne's work, nearer the c.1977 end of the date range than 1965.
errors: As literally written, 'Frob_ξ soit l'identité sur H_ξ(V)' is not right. F_∞ acts C-linearly on V_C and maps H^{p,q} to H^{q,p}. It is the antilinear composite F_∞ ⊗ (complex conjugation) that fixes the de Rham K-form (for K real at ξ). Presumably this composite is what is meant.

For a non-archimedean ξ, writing V ⊗ K̄_ξ ⊃ H_ξ(V)^{(p)} with a 'structure de Hodge' has no meaning without a period ring such as B_dR. The general-place notation is therefore at best heuristic. Most likely only archimedean places are intended.
Calling G° (rather than its image in GL(V)) the Galois group of the Hodge structure is loose. The text itself corrects this to 'Im G°'.

ideas.what: Hodge realization of a motive at a complex place: a de Rham K-form inside V_C with its Hodge filtration, making the Betti realization a Q-Hodge structure
ideas.modern_name: Hodge/de Rham realization; systems of realizations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Hodge II, 1971; Valeurs de fonctions L, 1979); Jannsen (mixed realizations, 1990)

ideas.what: The Mumford–Tate group of the Hodge realization is the image of the motivic Galois group G° in GL(V)
ideas.modern_name: Mumford–Tate group as image of the motivic Galois group (Hodge conjecture ⇒ equality)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mumford (1966), Deligne, Serre ('Propriétés conjecturales des groupes de Galois motiviques', 1994)

ideas.what: At a real place, an element Frob_ξ = F_∞ of G(Q) acting as an involution, compatible with polarization and Hodge structure
ideas.modern_name: Frobenius at infinity F_∞; real Hodge structures

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly casts the archimedean realizations as data attached to every place of K, including a Frobenius-at-infinity element in G(Q) for real places. This is the 'Frobenius at all places' picture of the motivic Galois group, which the literature credits to Deligne and Serre. It confirms that he envisaged infinite places on the same footing as finite ones inside the motivic Galois formalism.
missed.quote: Si ξ est réelle, on a une involution dans V provenant de l'élément Frob_ξ de G(Q)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical attribution only. The mathematics is standard today (Deligne 1979, Serre 1994).

missed.claim: The second block writes the Hodge filtration over K̄_ξ for an arbitrary place ξ, with a tree of completions. This hints, very speculatively, at a uniform Hodge-type realization at p-adic places as well, which is what p-adic Hodge theory (Fontaine) later supplied. The thread is not developed on the page.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only of historical interest, and only if confirmed by neighbouring pages of the notebook.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean but standard sketch of the Hodge realization of the motivic Galois group, with Mumford–Tate group equal to Im G° and F_∞ at real places. These ideas are well documented in Deligne and Serre. The page's interest is mainly as evidence of Grothendieck's own formulation, and its date is uncertain.
transcription_corrections: Top line: 'et prise p' likely reads 'et places p' / 'en des places' (uncertain); the parenthetical is barely legible.
'faisceau de Hodge' is more likely 'structure de Hodge' or 'réseau de Hodge'.
'on veut peut-être que Frob_ξ de forme hermitienne' is garbled; probably 'on veut peut-être que, par rapport à la forme hermitienne sur V̄_ξ, Frob_ξ soit l'identité sur H_ξ(V)'.
The left-margin diagram shows completions K_{ξ1}, K_{ξ2}, K_{ξ3} above K above Q.
